story.intro: {name} is a {layer} dictionary: it says what the names in IFC models mean{hasExample, select, yes {, e.g. “{raw}” means {term}} other {}}. Rules and classifications work with these meanings instead of the raw names, so the same rules work on models from any office, in any language. It changes quantities only through the rules that use the meanings.
story.knows: It knows <entries>{nameCount, plural, one {# name} other {# names}}</entries>{partial, select, yes { ({exact} exactly, {loose} by their start, a part or a pattern)} other {}}, defines <terms>{termCount, plural, one {# meaning of its own} other {# meanings of its own}}</terms>{readers, plural, =0 {} one { and reads <extractors>values out of names in # way</extractors> (thickness, strength class…)} other { and reads <extractors>values out of names in # ways</extractors> (thickness, strength class…)}}. <names>Names in the model</names> shows what each name in a model version means and lets you answer the ones not understood.
story.layers: When several dictionaries know a name, the most specific wins: your answer in the project (BoQ › Questions), then project, company and global dictionaries. Within one dictionary an exact name wins over “starts with”, then a pattern, then “contains”.

targets.term: a name to look up (its meaning)

about.title: About this dictionary
about.name: Name
about.idHint: How the dictionary names itself in the document; Names in the model shows it as where a meaning comes from.
about.layerHint: When several dictionaries know a name, project wins over company, company over global.

layerOptions.company: company: our office’s names and codes

terms.hint: The meanings (terms) rules and classifications work with: the clean words names are translated into. A meaning that is a kind of another counts as it: a rule for “material is a kind of concrete” also takes {example}. Most meanings come with the global dictionary; add your own here when your office has a word the others lack.
terms.empty: No meanings of its own: its names point to meanings other dictionaries define.
terms.name: Name
terms.broaderHint: Rules for the broader meaning also take this one.
terms.idHint: What rules and other dictionaries write, e.g. {example}. Renaming updates the names here that use it.
terms.retiredLabel: Keep for old answers, do not offer it any more
terms.valuesHint: Values rules may use, e.g. density_kg_m3 for weight by volume.
terms.linksHint: E.g. a bSDD URI or a Uniclass Pr code.

entries.hint: Each line here says: when a model names something like this, it means that. An exact name wins over “starts with”, then a pattern, then “contains”. Capitals and accents are ignored unless set otherwise. The quickest way to add names is Names in the model, with a model version picked.
entries.select: Select a name, or add one.
entries.rowSub: {fields} {match}{hasWhen, select, yes { · only in some cases} other {}}
entries.onlyWhenHint: Optional. The same name can mean different things on different elements: “CT” is ceramic tile only when {example}.
entries.moreSummary: · where it came from, note, id

sources.ai_confirmed: an AI suggestion a person confirmed

extractors.hint: Values written in names: a thickness in “Wall 25cm”, a strength class in “C30/37”, Revit’s family and type in “Family:Type:123”. Each reader is a pattern (a regular expression); each named part of it, written {syntax}, gives one value. Names in the model shows what is read from each name of a model version. Measured values from the geometry win unless a reader says otherwise.
extractors.select: Select a reader, or add one.
extractors.patternHint: JavaScript syntax; name each part you want: {example} reads the number before “cm” as part t.
extractors.override: overwrite them (usually not: geometry wins over names)
extractors.noParts: The pattern has no named parts yet.
extractors.noPart: no part named “{name}” in the pattern

names.noProjects: No project to take a model from yet. Upload an IFC model in a project, then come back.
names.noModels: This project has no models yet.
names.noReadyVersion: This model has no processed version yet.
names.pickHint: Pick a model version to see the names it uses.
names.intro: Every material and type name in {file}, and what it means. Give a name a term and it is saved in this dictionary ({layer} layer); every model with the same name is then understood.
names.worthHint: Names marked “worth answering” affect how elements are measured or coded; a BoQ run asks about them. The others can stay as they are.
names.notWorthHint: None of the names not understood yet affects measuring (door, window and furniture sizes rarely need a meaning); a BoQ run will not ask about them. Give them a term only if your rules or codes should use it.
names.removeHereTitle: Remove this name from this dictionary
names.higher: A {layer} dictionary answers this first; an answer here would not be used.
